mbm-1776.clue: My best bargain came with three keys.
mbm-1776.quote: I bought a battered tin cashbox at a flea market. Inside were three tiny keys and a dried daisy, no cash. My niece and I have been inventing shops for those keys ever since.

mbm-1777.clue: I can hear the orange tree on the radio.
mbm-1777.quote: My antenna runs past the kitchen window. A branch brushes it, and my first contact always asks if the oranges are ripe yet. I mailed her a drawing of the first blossom.

mbm-1778.clue: The marshmallow invents its own animal.
mbm-1778.quote: While the campfire cooled we toasted marshmallows and guessed what shape they'd sag into. I got an elephant complete with trunk. My cousin ate the evidence before the camera was ready.

mbm-1779.clue: We hung our shoes by the ears.
mbm-1779.quote: The camp fox stole a shoelace. We strung the rest of our shoes along the tent line by their loops. In the lantern light our little tent looked like a shop for sleeping bats.

mbm-1780.clue: There's a postcard from five streets away.
mbm-1780.quote: I spent all night tracking down a faint radio signal and finally spoke to a voice who knew the weather surprisingly well. He lived across town. We walked our confirmation cards to the bakery and swapped.

mbm-1781.clue: I used the zipper to make a railway.
mbm-1781.quote: An old jacket had just enough blue cloth for the sky in my quilt. I curved its long silver zipper across the hills. My niece runs the little engine up and down before she goes to sleep.

mbm-1782.quote: The first baby blanket I crocheted had one wave running the wrong way. My sister pointed to it and said that's where the salmon goes home. I sewed on one tiny silver fish.

mbm-1783.clue: The guest book is in my chalk bag.
mbm-1783.quote: I sketch the view from the top while my climbing partner slips out of climbing shoes. I keep every folded drawing in a tin. There's an entire cliff in there, one crumpled summit at a time.

mbm-1784.clue: I used to think every pilot waved at me.
mbm-1784.quote: I watched landings beside my granddad's red umbrella. When it finally wore out, a pilot from the club asked where our red spot had gone. We patched it together.

mbm-1785.clue: I took the long run for the tiny red door.
mbm-1785.quote: A warming hut on our hill has a painted mouse door beside the real one. I skied back the next weekend with my little cousin so she could knock. Somebody inside squeaked.

mbm-1786.clue: My best patch didn't need an iron.
mbm-1786.quote: I tore my brand-new overalls on a bicycle pedal. I sewed a little fabric bicycle right over the rip. Now my neighbor tells people it came through from the other side.

mbm-1787.clue: There's a propeller in my pencil sharpener.
mbm-1787.quote: I taped paper wings to an ordinary pencil to draw the planes at the airfield. The nose got shorter all summer. My friend said we should log the little aircraft's retirement flight.

mbm-1788.clue: I'm the only tree who gets a curtain call.
mbm-1788.quote: I played a willow in our community play and learned all the lines. On the night the lead lost his place, I rustled the right first word. At bows he came back and shook my branch.

mbm-1789.clue: I paint the underside before the wings.
mbm-1789.quote: I built a bright green model airship for a library display. The smallest visitors would see it from below, so I painted a whole koi pond on the belly. They found it before the grown-ups did.

mbm-1790.clue: My apron has a pocket the size of a seed packet.
mbm-1790.quote: I sewed it for my neighbour who gardens in wooden clogs. She wore it all through spring and gave me a tomato that grew from the packet in that pocket.

mbm-1791.clue: I play the shortest solo in the band.
mbm-1791.quote: When the bridge drops quiet, I strike the triangle once. My father drove a full hour to hear that note. From the back I saw him lift one finger right on cue.

mbm-1792.clue: The castle hole keeps my change.
mbm-1792.quote: My first putt vanished through a slot in the castle. I knelt to look and found three other balls and a foreign coin. The owner let me keep the coin if I set the prisoners free.

mbm-1793.clue: My favorite cut is the part that falls out.
mbm-1793.quote: I cut a row of swallows into red tissue for the market. The little scraps were perfectly good birds, so my sister glued them to our shopping list. We brought home six swallows and onions.

mbm-1794.clue: One sleeve knows which way to turn.
mbm-1794.quote: I practiced a ballroom turn by hanging my good shirt on the coat stand and leading it round the room. When my partner saw the trailing sleeve she pinned it up and said even a shirt should have good posture.

mbm-1795.clue: Try throwing toward the laundry line.
mbm-1795.quote: We hang a ribbon from the line to read the wind before a long disc throw. A sock blew down and curled around the ribbon. I sent the disc right through the sock's shadow.

mbm-1796.clue: I keep the ferry stamp on the first page.
mbm-1796.quote: I bought a book on a trip and the ferry clerk stamped its blank endpaper when I couldn't find my ticket. Every time I open it the voyage starts before chapter one.

mbm-1797.clue: The paint under the tape belongs to my niece.
mbm-1797.quote: I let her stick masking tape across my blank canvas any way she liked. When we peeled it after painting our river, the white lines made a second, sillier river. She claimed that one.

mbm-1798.clue: Nobody can steal the little bakery.
mbm-1798.quote: My friend's toddler claimed the wooden bakery from our board game and took it to bed. We play every other square as usual. At closing time we knock gently on her bedroom door to collect the rent.

mbm-1799.clue: I can stack the whole family in the cupboard.
mbm-1799.quote: I made nesting bowls, one each for us, with the smallest one for Gran's marmalade. She likes to take them all out just to put her bowl on top.

mbm-1800.clue: I wait for the blue kite to go by.
mbm-1800.quote: On sunny afternoons I stretch out on the dune with my radio. A kite maker tests his newest kite above the beach. I close one eye and use the aerial like a measuring stick.
